user.title: Find or add a local TP-Link/Kasa/Tapo device
user.description: Enter a device host for manual setup, or leave it blank to scan. Leave the discovery target blank to automatically scan enabled Home Assistant interface networks using their actual CIDR subnet masks. For a routed device VLAN enter its CIDR, e.g. 172.20.0.0/16; no separate mask is needed. CIDR scans can take several minutes.

data.host: Device IP address or hostname (leave blank to scan)
data.scan_target: Network to scan (optional CIDR or IPv4 address; blank = automatic)

dl100_session.title: Import DL100 local session
dl100_session.description: Legacy session import. If a previously saved encrypted LAN session cannot be verified, Tapo Local offers fresh owner-account authorization instead of requiring manual import.

smart_credentials.title: Local device authentication
smart_credentials.description: This device uses an authenticated local protocol. Enter the TP-Link account credentials currently authorized for the device. Tapo Local uses them only to verify the device locally and stores only python-kasa's protocol-specific credential hash after setup.

dl100_credentials.title: DL100 session authorization required
dl100_credentials.description: The Tapo DL100 does not provide a fully local method to create its DLKLAP session. Enter the TP-Link/Tapo owner account credentials once. Tapo Local uses them to create the required session and stores them privately in Home Assistant so you are not asked again. After setup, normal status, lock, and unlock actions are sent directly from Home Assistant to the lock over your local network. If the DL100 later invalidates its session, Home Assistant may briefly use the saved credentials to renew that session automatically in the background.

reconfigure.title: Change device IP address
reconfigure.description: Enter the new device IP address or hostname. Tapo Local checks the same device identity and keeps the existing entry and entities. If a DL100 rejects its saved session, the integration will try to renew it using previously authorized owner credentials; renewal may briefly contact TP-Link services.

reconfigure_dl100_credentials.title: Reauthorize DL100 at the new address
reconfigure_dl100_credentials.description: The DL100 saved LAN session was rejected or is missing. Enter the TP-Link/Tapo owner credentials authorized for this lock to obtain a fresh encrypted LAN session. Account verification may briefly use TP-Link services. The current IP and existing saved session remain unchanged if authorization or local verification fails.

discovered.title: Devices found on the network
discovered.description: Choose a device to add. {already_configured} previously configured Tapo Local device(s) were found and hidden. No existing entries will be changed.

error.cannot_connect: Unable to connect to the device using its forced local protocol.
error.dependency_unavailable: Tapo Local could not prepare its required local-control runtime. No device commands were attempted. Check Settings > System > Repairs and the Home Assistant log for the exact dependency error.
error.dl100_session_missing: No usable saved DL100 session was found. Reauthorize the lock with its owner account credentials to establish a new encrypted LAN session.
error.dl100_session_invalid: The DL100 session import file exists but does not contain a valid saved DLKLAP session.
error.dl100_session_rejected: The DL100 rejected the saved encrypted LAN session or returned an unexpected local response. Check that the lock is reachable and awake; retry or reauthorize the session. The existing device address was not changed.
error.unsupported_device: The device responded locally, but its device family or Home Assistant platform is not supported by this Tapo Local build.
error.invalid_auth: The device rejected the supplied credentials.
error.credentials_hash_unavailable: The device authenticated locally, but python-kasa did not provide a reusable credential hash. Tapo Local will not store the plaintext password.
error.dl100_auth_failed: DL100 authorization failed at an unidentified step. See Home Assistant logs for the precise stage; existing configuration remains unchanged.
error.invalid_host: Enter a valid IP address or hostname, without a URL, port, or path.
error.device_identity_unavailable: This entry has no verifiable device identity. The address was not changed to avoid connecting to a different device.
error.wrong_device: A different device responded at that address. The existing IP address was not changed.
error.invalid_scan_target: Enter an RFC1918 IPv4 address or CIDR from /16 to /32 (for example 172.20.0.0/16), or 255.255.255.255. Wider and public networks are blocked.
error.scan_failed: The network scan failed. Check Home Assistant networking and try manual IP setup.
error.no_devices_found: No unconfigured Tapo devices answered. Auto mode uses Home Assistant's enabled interface CIDRs; for routed VLANs like 172.20.0.0/16, specify that CIDR directly. Legacy Kasa switches are also checked using TCP 9999.
error.invalid_selection: Select a device from the current discovery results.
error.dl100_cloud_login_failed: DL100 owner-account login failed. Check account credentials, TP-Link cloud availability, and any account verification requirements. Details appear in Home Assistant logs.
error.dl100_cloud_device_failed: DL100 identification failed: the account did not return one identifiable DL100 device. Confirm the account owns the lock and review Home Assistant logs.
error.dl100_control_key_failed: DL100 owner authorization reached the control-key service but no usable control key was issued. Check Home Assistant logs for the HTTP status or error code.
error.dl100_local_handshake_failed: DL100 local encrypted handshake failed. Check that the lock is awake and reachable on TCP port 80; Home Assistant logs identify the failed handshake.

abort.no_devices_found: No devices are available from this scan; restart setup to try again.
abort.scan_not_started: No scan is currently running. Restart the integration setup to scan again.

progress.scanning: Scanning the requested network for Tapo/Kasa devices

python_kasa_dependency.title: Tapo Local could not prepare its runtime dependencies
python_kasa_dependency.description: Tapo Local requires {requirement}. Home Assistant was unable to leave that runtime in a working state. {detail}
